name: Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers, higher-order energy, and (algorithmic) Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa
description: BSG: a set with additive energy at least |A|^3/K contains a large subset A' with small doubling. PFR (Gowers-Green-Manners-Tao): in F_2^n, doubling K implies A is covered by poly(K) translates of a subspace of size at most |A|. Arunachalam-Castro-Silva-Dutt give a poly(n)-time randomized algorithm (O~(n^4)) that finds the subspace. Shao and Shkredov higher-order energy results were not read.
authors_year_venue: BSG: Balog-Szemeredi 1994, Gowers 1998 (classical, cited in 2509.02338 Thm 2.5). PFR: W. T. Gowers, B. Green, F. Manners, T. Tao, 'On a conjecture of Marton', Annals of Mathematics 201(2):515-549, 2025 (as cited). Algorithmic PFR: S. Arunachalam, D. Castro-Silva, A. Dutt, T. Gur, arXiv:2509.02338 (Sep 2025). Shao-Shkredov: not read [uncertain].
status_and_verification: GGMT25 peer-reviewed per citation (not itself read). arXiv:2509.02338 preprint read via alphaXiv: abstract, Sec 1-1.3, Sec 2 (definitions, BSG statement Thm 2.5, Plunnecke, Ruzsa covering), Lemma 3.1, Thm 4.1 proof, Thm 4.5 statement. Shao-Shkredov higher-order energy and Z-valued BSG/PFR transfers were NOT read primary-source. [uncertain]
key_theorem_or_bound: Thm 1.1 (GGMT): exists polynomial P0 such that A subset F_2^n with |A+A| <= K|A| is covered by at most P0(K) translates of a subspace V of size at most |A|. Thm 1.2 (algorithmic PFR): O~(n^4)-time randomized algorithm, O(log|A|) random samples and O~(log^2|A|) queries, success prob 2/3, outputs V of size <= |A| with A covered by P1(K) translates. Thm 4.1: samples O(log|A|+K), queries 2^{O(K)} log^2|A| loglog|A|, time K^{O(log K)} n^4 log n. Thm 2.5 (BSG): E(A) >= |A|^3/K gives A' subset A with |A'| >= |A|/P_BSG^(1)(K), |A'+A'| <= P_BSG^(2)(K)|A|. Thm 2.4 Freiman-Ruzsa: |span A| <= 2^{2K}/(2K) |A|.
regime_exponents: K treated as constant (or at most poly) independent of n. For the repo, relevant K would be 2^{epsilon n} (exponential energy). Algorithm queries 2^{O(K)} so effectively only constant K. No statement about 0.311n/0.5n/0.661n; those are the repo's thresholds.
proof_type_and_tools: PFR: entropic methods (non-algorithmic). Algorithmic version: algorithmizing Green-Tao/Lovett equivalence PFR iff polynomial Gowers U^3 inverse theorem, using stabilizer learning (Chen-Gong-Ye-Zhang), dequantized by Briet-Castro-Silva quadratic Goldreich-Levin; Ruzsa covering lemma; Freiman isomorphism via random linear map (dense model).
quantitative_loss: BSG: polynomial in K (poly(K) losses in size and doubling, exponents unspecified in the text read). PFR: polynomial P0(K), 2^{O(K)} queries in the algorithm. If K is exponential in n (high energy at 2^{epsilon n}), polynomial losses become exponential: BSG yields a subset of size |A|/K^{c} and doubling K^{c'}, which with K=2^{epsilon n} is vacuous unless c epsilon is small; and 2^{O(K)} queries is doubly exponential. So it does NOT survive exponential energy without a separate argument.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst case over all sets A in F_2^n with doubling K, randomized algorithm needing sample and query access. No assumption about random inputs.
coefficient_set: F_2^n (characteristic 2) for PFR/algorithmic PFR; BSG holds in any abelian group; integer Z version of PFR is not provided here (Z requires Freiman-type GAPs, not subspaces). Subset-sum coefficient sets {0,1} appear only through Z embedding, not covered.
subset_size_regime: Sets A (arbitrary size) in a group; not subset sums. To apply to subset sums, A must be the set of k-subset indicator vectors or of half-sums, with k=Theta(n); no theorem in the read papers addresses that.
relevance_to_Nc: If many equal-sum disjoint pairs of Theta(n)-subsets exist (N_c large), the set family has additive energy about N_c in the group of sums; BSG converts energy >= |A|^3/K into a large subset with small doubling, then PFR/Freiman gives structure. The branch 'large N_c -> structure -> algorithm' is the C1 large-bin branch. The transfer needs Z-valued versions and exponential K.
relevance_to_Dstar: Few distinct balanced half-sums (D* small) means the set of half-sums has small doubling-like growth; BSG/PFR would give a subspace/GAP covering structure and constrain D*. Direct implication D* >= 2^{0.311n} for hard instances is not proved here [uncertain]; PFR is F_2^n only, so for Z must use Freiman/Bilu or Gowers-Green-Manners-Tao integer variants.
applicability_gap: (1) Exponential K: polynomial losses of BSG and PFR become exponential; and the 2^{O(K)} query bound is useless. (2) F_2^n vs Z: the algorithmic PFR is over F_2^n; transferring to subset sums in Z needs a Freiman model in Z where covering by GAPs has exponential dimension/volume losses. (3) Energy of A (pairs a+b=c+d) vs N_c (disjoint equal-sum pairs of Theta(n)-subsets) differ by overlapping-support pairs. (4) Shao-Shkredov higher energy not checked.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Sets with high energy but no subspace structure: sets A = V union Sidon-like pieces (energy dominated by V, so BSG subset is V); near-extremal doubling examples (union of subspace plus random points) show polynomial loss is necessary in PFR (GGMT). For subset sums, rank-d GAP with random generators have small D*; Sidon/AP-free sets have minimal energy. Not verified on this repo's families.
dependency_chain: Energy (Shao-Shkredov higher-order) -> BSG (poly(K) subset with small doubling) -> PFR/algorithmic PFR (F_2^n subspace cover) or Freiman (Z) -> constructive Freiman (Randolph-Wegrzycki) -> algorithm. Also Plunnecke-Ruzsa for sumset growth.
constructiveness: Algorithmic PFR is constructive: O~(n^4) time, O(log|A|) samples, O~(log^2|A|) queries (classical), O(n^3) quantum; lower bounds Omega(n^2) queries classical, Omega(n) quantum. Cost 2^{O(K)} queries makes it only practical for constant K. BSG constructive version by Chan-Lewenstein 2015 (cited in 2407.18228).
lean_formalizable: PFR was formalized in Lean 4 with mathlib (not mathlib-free); BSG elementary combinatorial proof is plausible in a mathlib-free setting (Cauchy-Schwarz, popular differences) but PFR entropy proof is heavy [uncertain].
computational_check: 2509.02338 reports no experiments (theory). Repo could compute additive energy of the set of balanced half-sums at n<=40 and test BSG-type extraction (greedy dense subset with small doubling), comparing log2 E / log2 |A|^3.
next_experiment: Compute E(S) and |S+S|/|S| for S = set of half-sum vectors of Theta(n)-subsets for random and rank-d GAP instances at n<=30; check whether log_2 K scales linearly in n (exponential energy) and how large a BSG subset one can greedily extract.
open_issues: Dependence on K in algorithmic PFR remains 2^{O(K)} queries (open whether poly(K)); no integer-group algorithmic PFR; Shao-Shkredov higher-order energy statements not verified; BSG polynomial exponents not tracked.
